items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: That was a band in the seventies. And all we did for a year that I was with them... and we had a vocalist that could scat great, Barbie... She could scat great, sang really well

ctx.x: Wow. It must have made an impression on you at the time, for you to remember that.

I remember just the whole night. I can still see that room right now, yeah. Things like that, I just never ever forget. Plateaus. When you crack those certain plateaus, you never forget it. At least I haven’t. I can remember all the points where I found out the switch — I just moved a level. And this was my first one, to play a solo that I felt like appropriate, imaginative and the whole bit, and even the cats that night, I mean just when the set was over they were all like, oh man. You were burning, man. I…

Rankin. She could scat great, sang really well, and would learn her parts just like any other horn player would. And we started doing like Ella charts, all these hip things, the stuff from Nancy Wilson/Cannonball Adderley.
